sources.title: Data Sources
questions: The project’s data source are: Publicly-available project data (e.g. project description, posts, and the like), which is inherently public but is under scrutiny in the case study due to the hackers releasing such data without following Patreon’s TOS. Private communications and Personally-identifiable Information (emails), which are considered Special Category Data under GDPR Patreon’s Codebase, which is legally sensitive proprietary data.

The researchers originally tried to scrape Patreon’s publicly-accessible data  but failed to properly do so due to technical issues. All of the mentioned data was made available in the data dump that was shared by Patreon’s hackers.
Given the illegal method used to source this data, accessing and using the leaked data dump for any purpose (research included) is legally impermissible and is highly discouraged.

limitations.title: Limitations in data sources
questions: On the researcher’s side, technical difficulties such as Patreon’s website not having a good scraping hook limited their data scraping attempts. The researchers also noted that should they want to access the data dump, they would have limited capability to distinguish between public and private files while sanitizing their research dataset, especially as the dump is a single file that contains all files.
The hack also calls into question the ethics of using such data - do the researchers use the more complete but illegally sourced data in their research or do they stick with their scraped data?

The apparent ethical dilemma in this case study manifests in the limitations, as the researchers debate on using (or not using) complete but illegally sourced data. Assessing the ethics and legality of such an action (to be discussed in the next section) is crucial on whether they want to address these limitations or leave them as is.

sharing.title: Sharing data with others
questions: As the data dump contains both publicly-available and legally sensitive and proprietary data, it is legally impermissible to share it to other entities and publish such data.
The researchers should not share nor publish the data.

ethical-legislative.title: Ethical and legislative context
questions: To discuss the ethics behind research integrity and privacy and consent, we use Kantian ethics, utilitarianism and Nissenbaum’s theory of Contextual integrity. If the researchers decide to use the data, we use rights-based ethics and Floridi’s Information ethics to discuss if it’s possible to balance academic transparency and harm mitigation (in the context of the hacking victims)

To discuss the ethics behind research integrity and privacy and consent, we use Articles 5, 6, and 14 of GDPR. To discuss the legal consequences in potentially using hacked data, we use GDPR Article 25 and the US Common Rule (45 CFR Part 46). Lastly, IP and copyright laws are also relevant as the data includes Patreon’s codebase.

As the researchers ultimately decided to not use the data, these ethical and legal frameworks serve as references in analyzing future similar actions, as well as the appropriate legal consequences to be given for academics that violate them.

rights.title: Rights around data sources
questions: Despite the fact that the data was already available publicly online, the act of gathering it from the public domain is not by itself problematic. However its use is highly debatable. The raw Patreon data was never supposed to be made public and entities other than Patreon should only have the sole rights of its use.

Hence, the data collected from being shared by Patreon’s hackers is owned by Patreon and shall only be rightfully used by Patreon. All others who have the leaked data shall have no permission at all to use them for their own benefit.

It is clear from the outset that the data exposed by hackers, no matter how impactful it may be, does not warrant to be used by other entities. As the article says, these are the data we want, but we don’t need. Organizations should adhere to the ethical standards of research and it starts with the collection of data.

reasons.title: Your reasons for using data
questions: The primary purpose of using the data is to understand the trends of crowdsourcing. Given that crowdsourcing is an event where ideas get pitched and willing donors support the said idea, it is imperative for the society to learn from successful crowdsourced projects. Online platforms like Patreon are one of the most prominent sources of data as these make crowdfunding more accessible all the time and all around the world.

The raw data that exposes not only the financial transactions but also private messages would further enrich the analysis of the research. This would in turn make the society better by knowing how to pitch properly and effectively to gain support from donors and patrons. However the data included is with private and identifiable information that will be subject to ethical issues when included in the study.

The researchers and the data scientists shall make sure to not use the leaked data at all, as this would effectively question the ethics of the research team. Instead, they must go through the albeit rigorous but acceptable way of data gathering and be subject to the ethics committee.

communicating.title: Communicating your purpose
questions: The first intent of using the leaked data is to promote the research of Patreon’s raw information to draw any and all possible potential interpretations of the dataset.
Based on the less-than-ethical means to provide this purpose with the vague messaging, it does not warrant the use of the leaked data to conform to the purpose.
It must be ensured that no research would mistake the purpose as a validation of the use of the data.

positive-effects.title: Positive effects on people
questions: This project can positively affect multiple groups, including creators on crowdfunding platforms, researchers studying digital labour and cultural production, and organisations interested in platform transparency and equitable creator compensation. By producing ethically grounded insights into long-term funding patterns, the research can help illuminate structural dynamics that shape creator sustainability and platform economies.

Positive impact can be measured through the clarity and usefulness of the research outputs—such as publications, briefings, and visualisations—that inform stakeholders and contribute to broader conversations about digital work, platform fairness, and creator livelihoods. Communicating findings openly and accessibly can extend this impact, especially by making results relevant to creators, policymakers, and digital rights communities.

negative-effects.title: Negative effects on people
questions: Using data originating from the 2015 Patreon breach could negatively affect individuals whose private information was exposed. The dataset contains sensitive elements (e.g., private messages, email addresses, passwords) that create a high risk of re-identification. Using this data—even for research—may violate users’ expectations of privacy and could contribute to further harm by legitimising the circulation of illegally obtained information.

The way the hacked dataset was acquired and circulated raises ethical, legal, and reputational risks. If the research draws on this data, users may feel targeted, profiled, or exploited. It may also appear that the researchers condone criminal data breaches, potentially undermining trust in academic research practices and in crowdfunding communities.

mitigations.title: Minimising negative impact
questions: Avoid the compromised dataset entirely and ensure that all data sources meet legal, ethical, and platform-specific requirements. Researchers should prioritise participant privacy, minimise data retention, and prevent the inadvertent exposure of sensitive information.

Limitations in the data should be mitigated by adopting transparent methodological frameworks. Security protocols must be implemented for any data handling. The team must ensure that any remaining public data collected cannot be linked back to identifiable users. Risk assessment should be ongoing, with regular review points.

engaging.title: Engaging with people
questions: In the context of IGBP, interested groups and individuals sent their videos to Savage and Miller for them to post to the IGBP channel. However the issue is that the channel is inherently subject to Youtube’s TOS, which restricts it to a limited number of videos since the year the channel was created.

No formal channels for appealing existed during that time, and so Savage and Miller found it hard to reach out to Youtube. It was only through the intervention of Chen that the issue was resolved in a questionable manner.
YouTube should also establish a communication channel to its creators, given that Chen’s intervention was just through their personal interest rather than from their professional capacity

openness.title: Openness and transparency
questions: The project can be highly open regarding its methodology, analytical approach, and ethical reasoning, especially that the decision is not to use hacked or illegally obtained data. While the underlying dataset cannot be published in full due to platform ownership and terms of service, the research process—including sampling strategies, limitations, and analytical methods—can be made publicly accessible.
Peer feedback can be incorporated and defined through academic workshops and conferences, internal review meetings, and sharing draft outputs with colleagues.
Publish a detailed methodology document outlining data sources, limitations, ethical decisions, and analytical procedures.

implementation.title: Ongoing implementation
questions: The research team shall make sure that they have ethically sourced the data that they collect. Using the exposed raw data of Patreon does legitimize criminal activity by setting a bad precedent for other researches using the same leaked dataset.
A rigorous training of data collection and data cleaning will be an important step to realize that given that data is being publicly available, it does not mean that it is always ethical to use them.

The ethics committee shall make sure to perform checks and balances to ensure all researches to be published have gone through a process of verifying the data sources and whether these sources are ethically sourced.

review.title: Reviews and iterations
questions: To adequately check the ethicality of the research, all researchers should be subjected to the ethics committee to identify whether they have violated any portion of their research, from data collection to interpretation of results.

The result of the research audit shall also be discussed with the team, and corresponding training shall be enforced not only to the sanctioned individual but also to the research team to prevent the recurrence of such ethical problems.

The data ethics canvas shall also be reviewed and updated whenever a research team has been found to be violating ethical guidelines. This ensures that the data ethics canvas will be maintained to suit the changing landscapes.

actions.title: Your actions
questions: The research should primarily reject the use of exposed and leaked data for it can jeopardize the authenticity of the research and the organization. The ethics committee shall prioritize that all of the company’s research articles comply with the necessary standards to ensure integrity.

The research team held liable on the grounds of the use of leaked data shall be investigated and undertake the necessary protocols to ensure that the research that the organization outputs not only shares valuable information but also would have no doubtful and questionable acts in any part of the research methodology.
